source.author: verg
source.text: Tum numina sancta precamur Palladis armisonae, quae prima accepit ovantis, et capita ante aras Phrygio velamur amictu; praeceptisque Heleni, dederat quae maxima, rite Iunoni Argivae iussos adolemus honores.
source.text_original: Tum numina sancta precamur / Palladis armisonae, quae prima accepit ovantis, / et capita ante aras Phrygio velamur amictu; / praeceptisque Heleni, dederat quae maxima, rite / Iunoni Argivae iussos adolemus honores.
source.text_english: Then we pray to the holy powers of armed Pallas, who first received the cheering celebrants, and we veil our heads before the altars with a Phrygian cloak; and, following Helenus’ instructions, which he had given as the chief of all, we duly pay the commanded honors to Argive Juno.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ergo umeros ductor sacro velatur amictu Aesoniamque capit pateram, quam munere gaudens liquerat hospitio pharetrasque rependerat auro Salmoneus, nondum ille furens, qui fingeret alti quadrifida trabe tela Iovis contraque ruenti aut Athon aut Rhodopen maestae nemora ardua Pisae aemulus et miseros ipse ureret Elidis agros.
reuse.text_original: ergo umeros ductor sacro velatur amictu / Aesoniamque capit pateram, quam munere gaudens / liquerat hospitio pharetrasque rependerat auro / Salmoneus, nondum ille furens, qui fingeret alti / quadrifida trabe tela Iovis contraque ruenti / aut Athon aut Rhodopen maestae nemora ardua Pisae / aemulus et miseros ipse ureret Elidis agros.
reuse.text_english: So the leader veils his shoulders with the sacred cloak and takes up the Aesonian bowl, which, rejoicing in the gift, Salmonius had left behind as a gift of hospitality and had repaid the quivers with gold, Salmonius, not yet that raging man who would fashion the weapons of high Jupiter from a split beam, and, rivaling him as he hurled against Athos or Rhodope the steep woods of mournful Pisa, would himself burn the wretched fields of Elis.
